subject: space station
title: What If the Space Station Sprang a Leak? In 2018 It Did

scenes.text: What if the space station sprang a leak? In 2018 it did. The crew slept through it.
August 29th, about 7 p.m. Eastern. Flight controllers see the cabin pressure slipping. It's slow, so they let the crew sleep.
Next morning the astronauts hunt for it. They trace it to a Russian Soyuz capsule docked to the station.
The hole is two millimeters wide. European astronaut Alexander Gerst reportedly covers it with his finger.
Then comes tape, and finally gauze soaked in sealant, pushed into the hole. The pressure holds.
Left alone, the leak would have emptied the station's air in about 18 days. Russia first blamed a micrometeoroid. NASA never confirmed that.

description:
What if the International Space Station started leaking air? On 29 August 2018, flight controllers noticed a slow pressure drop and let the crew sleep.
The next day the crew traced it to a 2-millimetre hole in the orbital module of the docked Soyuz MS-09. ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst reportedly held a finger over it before cosmonauts sealed it with tape, then gauze and epoxy. Unrepaired, the leak would have drained the station's air in about 18 days.
